patches.purpose: Safely repair verified CRLF migration checksums used by existing Windows Codex homes. Regenerated against rust-v0.172.0 (2026-11-28; the only conflict was an import line in migrations.rs), which still lacks an equivalent repair. Since 2026-10-22 it also keeps the fork out of the official Codex app's ~/.codex: with CODEX_HOME unset the Windows default home is Crossline's own (utils/home-dir crossline_default_home), and the repair skips databases directly in %USERPROFILE%/.codex (state is_official_codex_home_db).

build.lockfileNote: The rust-v0.172.0 tag records 174 workspace packages as 0.0.0; Cargo synchronized only those entries to 0.172.0 before the locked rebuild (git diff shows 174 version lines changed and nothing else, 2026-11-28).
build.binaryNote: Still the rust-v0.163.0 root build (2026-11-01, e4c45291…): the root has not been rebuilt from rust-v0.172.0. rust-v0.163.0 plus the fork's ~/.codex isolation (crossline_default_home, is_official_codex_home_db), built 2026-11-01 with cargo build --locked (17 min, rustc 1.95.0) in the worktree modest-nightingale-ea278c (branch fix/fork-codex-home-isolation-main; the 2026-10-22 build 43b258b2… of the same source on fix/fork-codex-home-isolation was never merged) and copied to this path, where the worker resolves it. Rust debug builds embed the absolute source path, so a build elsewhere has another hash; lockfileSha256 is the provenance proof. The root build before the isolation (e6300d7f…, 2026-10-20) stays accepted in CODEX_PREVIOUS_BINARY_SHA256 until the root's copy is replaced.
